summary_points: Document details: Title, client, project, document code, supplier code, revision, date, and signatures.
Important installation instructions include removing orange-painted parts, checking plug tightness, notifying LOINTEK for warranty work, and being cautious when entering system channels/shells.
Table of contents outlines sections on shipping/installation, start-up/operation, maintenance/reparations, and annexes with documentation and testing details.
Gasket replacement instructions provided
Installation requires true horizontal plane
Review Transport drawing for lifting information
Use nylon slings with rubber protection
Fixed supports need shims and proper elevation
All bolt elements must be correctly installed and tightened according to standard pairs for fixed supports, but not in sliding supports.
Piping connections should remove shipping covers and plugs before operation, and residual water should be removed through nozzles.
Nitrogen protection is crucial; personnel must avoid visual inspection of internals due to its colorless and odorless nature.
The system must be clean and free of foreign objects before starting operation.
All connections on the General Arrangement Drawing must be utilized unless otherwise approved by LOINTEK.
Pipelines should be blown before welding to equipment.
Corrosion protection requires maintaining nitrogen seal for long-term storage and protecting with a blanket after piping completion.
Any alterations or repairs should be made under LOINTEK's direction and in accordance with their procedures.
Hydrostatic testing instructions are provided in Annex 2 if required.
Close venting valves when filling the system.
Put Exchangers in Recirculation Mode with Cold Tank.
Circulate molten salt from Cold Tank, ensuring shell side temperature is at least 518 ºF (270ºC).
Increase HTF Temperature until molten salt Outlet Temperature is 370.8 ºF (388.22ºC), with a maximum heating rate of 18ºF/minute (10ºC/minute).
Close recirculation mode with cold tank and route molten salt to Hot Tank.
Increase gradually both flows until 100%, maintaining a heating rate of 50 ºF/minute (10ºC/minute).
Unit is now in “Nomal Charge Case”. Protect internals from corrosion and pitting during shutdown.
Welding must be performed using a qualified procedure, reviewed by a Notified Body.
Proper preheat, dryness, and cleanliness are crucial for welding.
Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger System bundles are heavy and easily damaged.
Shell removal requires careful handling with support steps.
Horizontal heaters need adequate cribbing at maximum spacing of 2m.
Chain hoists recommended for precise bundle height adjustment during insertion.
Cover exposed areas and shell openings with plastic to minimize corrosion.
Thorough inspection required before shell reinstallation.
Radiographic examination needed on carbon steel seams greater than 1-1/4" thick.
Bolted connections should be tightened uniformly in a staggered pattern.
Periodic checks recommended for bolted joints during the first six months of operation.
Torque values for SA-193-B7 studs are provided with a pre-load of 60% yield.
Disassembly requires protection to prevent parts from falling free or shifting.
Gasket selection should follow original design, and non-hardening compounds are recommended.
Locating tube failures involves collecting specific data on the failure location.
Tubesheet/tube end examination includes visual inspection and penetrant testing.
